LVKE.|149}}</noinclude>cities, and behold a man ful of leprosie, and seeing {{sc|Iesvs}}, and falling on his face, besought him saying, Lord, if thou vvilt, thou canst make me cleane. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=13}}† And stretching forth the hand, he {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Our Saviour often healeth by touching.}}∷ touched him, saying, I vvil. be thou made cleane. And immediatly the leprosie departed from him. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=14}}† And he commaunded him that he should tel no body, but, Goe, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''See S. Mat. Annot. c. 8, 4.''}}* shevv thy self to the Priest, and offer for thy cleansing {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Lev. 14, 2.''}}* as Moyses commaunded, for a testimonie to them.

{{verse|chapter=5|verse=15}}† But the bruite of him vvent abrode the more. and great multitudes came together to heare, and to be cured of their infirmities. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=16}}† And he retired into the desert, and praied.

{{verse|chapter=5|verse=17}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 9, 2. Mr. 2, 3.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Gospel vpō Friday in Whitsonvveeke.}}∷ And it came to passe one day, and he sate teaching. And there vvere Pharisees sitting and Doctors of Lavv that vvere come out of euery tovvne of Galilee and Ievvrie and Hierusalem: and the vertue of our Lord vvas to heale them. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=18}}† And behold men carying in a bed a man that had the palsey: and they sought to bring him in, and to lay him before him. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=19}}† And not finding on vvhich side they might bring him in for the multitude, they {{sup|‖}} vvent vp vpon the roofe, and through the tiles let him dovvne vvith the bed into the middes, before {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=20}}† {{sup|‖}} VVhose faith vvhen he savv, he said, Man, thy sinnes are forgiuen thee. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=21}}† And the Scribes and Pharisees began to thinke, saying, Who is this that speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgiue sinnes, but only God? {{verse|chapter=5|verse=22}}† And when {{sc|Iesvs}} knevve their cogitations, ansvvering he said to them, VVhat doe you thinke in your hartes? {{verse|chapter=5|verse=23}}† VVhich is easier to say, Thy sinnes are forgiuen thee: or to say, Arise, and vvalke? {{verse|chapter=5|verse=24}}† but that you may knovv that {{sup|‖}} the sonne of man hath povver in earth to forgiue sinnes (he said to the sicke of the palsey) I say to thee, Arise, take vp thy bed, and goe into thy house. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=25}}† And forthvvith rising vp before them, he tooke that wherein he lay: and he vvent into his house, magnifying God. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=26}}† And al vvere astonied: and they magnified God. And they vvere replenished vvith feare, saying, That vve haue seen maruelous things to day.⊣ {{verse|chapter=5|verse=27}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 9, 9. Mr. 2, 14.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Gospel vpō S. Matthevves eue Septēb. 20.}}∷ And after these things he vvent forth, and savv a Publican called Leui, sitting at the Custome-house, and he said to him, Folovv me. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=28}}† And {{sup|‖}} leauing al things, he rose and folovved him. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=29}}† and Leui made him a great feast in his house: and there vvas a great multitude of Publicans, and of others that vvere sitting at the table vvith them. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=30}}† And their Pharisees and<noinclude>{{rh||T iij|Scribes}}</noinclude>
